title: Ines and the Confession
premise: Coral Dravenmoor, the reclusive archivist of Saint Verity's Cathedral, has spent a decade cataloguing the town of Hollowmere's secrets—until he finds the diary of missing schoolteacher Ines Marchetti continuing entries dated years after her disappearance. Following the diary's coded references to a ledger hidden in the cathedral's locked crypt, Coral uncovers a confession implicating the town's founding families in her murder and a cover-up that reaches into his own past. As the statute of limitations nears expiry and those implicated close ranks, Coral must choose between the invisible safety of his archives and exposing the truth; in the end, he opens the crypt publicly on the statute's final day, freeing both Ines's memory and himself into an unlikely found family among the townsfolk who help him.
about_author: Odile Delacroix is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent fifteen years among ledgers, crypts, and confidences before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about quiet people who discover that silence is never neutral.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Absence
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He catalogs the cathedral's tenth annual memorial file for Ines Marchetti, revealing his ritualized invisibility and precise mind. A donated box of effects includes her diary—its final entry dated three years after she vanished. Emotional beat: unease cracking open routine.

chapters.title: Ink After Death
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Forensic caution wars with obsession as he verifies the handwriting against archived letters; it is unmistakably Ines's. The last entry mentions 'the ledger under the ninth stone.' Emotional beat: vertigo—the dead do not write.

chapters.title: Locked Crypt, Open Wound
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He petitions Dean Ambrose Fenn to reopen the sealed crypt; the dean refuses with uncharacteristic sharpness. Coral notices fresh mortar dust on the crypt stairs. Emotional beat: first suspicion that the church itself is complicit.

chapters.title: The Ninth Stone
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, intercut with diary excerpts. Night visit to the crypt; he finds the ninth stone hollow but empty except for a wax rubbing of ledger columns. Someone got there first. Emotional beat: dread and exhilaration in equal measure.

chapters.title: Miss Pell and the Borrowed Light
chapters.summary: Tamsin Pell's POV introduced—a young locksmith's apprentice who once caught Coral breaking into the vestry and kept his secret. She becomes his reluctant ally, reading the rubbing as a merchant cipher. Emotional beat: the first thread of belonging.

chapters.title: Entries That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The diary's post-disappearance entries describe ordinary days—market, rain, a dog named Bracken—suggesting Ines lived hidden, not died. But one entry names 'the Vane brothers' with fear. Emotional beat: hope complicated by menace.

chapters.title: Founding Families
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Research in his own archive maps the Vanes, the Quill family, and Judge Harrow onto the ledger's column headings: payments spanning decades. The town's charity was hush money. Emotional beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: A Visitor Who Signs Nothing
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A lawyer representing the Vane estate requests 'routine' access to restricted files. Coral stonewalls using archival bureaucracy as armor, then finds his office searched. Emotional beat: invisibility failing him.

chapters.title: Bracken
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She traces the diary's dog to Edith Quill, elderly and dying, who once kept a dog named Bracken—and who whispers that Ines 'stayed where they couldn't look.' Emotional beat: tenderness toward the town's buried kindnesses.

chapters.title: Where They Couldn't Look
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Re-reading the diary spatially, he realizes the entries' marginal marks map to the cathedral itself—Ines hid inside the one place the families would never desecrate. Emotional beat: awe at her audacity.

chapters.title: The Reliquary Wall
chapters.summary: Coral and Tamsin's POV alternating. Behind a false reliquary panel they find the true ledger and a second journal: Ines witnessed the Vanes disposing of a body—not hers—in the fen. Emotional beat: horror reframing everything.

chapters.title: Whose Body in the Fen
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Old coroner records show an unidentified drowned man ruled accidental, signed by Judge Harrow. Ines fled because no one would believe her. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger and fury at the machinery of respectability.

chapters.title: Dean Fenn's Confession
chapters.summary: Fenn's POV. Cornered by Coral, the dean admits his predecessor burned evidence to protect endowments—but insists Ines left alive, escorted out by someone he never named. Emotional beat: shame wearing the mask of duty.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Tamsin discovers the concealment charges expire in nineteen days; after that, only moral justice remains. The lawyer's visits intensify; Coral receives an anonymous note: 'Archives burn easily.' Emotional beat: the clock becoming a character.

chapters.title: Edith's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Dying Edith gives Tamsin a letter from Ines she was paid to hold for thirty years: proof Ines lived, and a condition—publish only if someone finally asked. Coral asks. Emotional beat: inheritance of trust.

chapters.title: The Fire
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. An arson attempt guts the archive wing at night; Coral, working late, barely escapes, saving the diary and ledger in a document case. The town watches its archivist stand in the smoke. Emotional beat: the invisible man made visible.

chapters.title: Witnesses Come Forward
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided—Fenn, Tamsin, the locksmith, a retired constable. Shamed by the fire, townspeople bring Coral their own suppressed papers. Emotional beat: found family assembling around a table of evidence.

chapters.title: The Vane Account
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Decoding completes: payments trace to the night of the drowning, including a bribe to the escort who took Ines away—signed E.Q. Edith Quill saved her. Emotional beat: the conspiracy unraveling into individual choices, good and bad.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days Later
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On the statute's final morning, Coral breaks the crypt seal publicly before press, police, and the assembled town, reading Ines's confession aloud over the ninth stone. Emotional beat: climax—truth as ceremony, courage as paperwork.

chapters.title: What the Law Cannot Do
chapters.summary: Detective Inspector Sorrel's POV. Legal charges lapse, but the exposure forces resignations, restitution, and a reopened inquest for the drowned man. Justice arrives sideways, imperfect, real. Emotional beat: sober satisfaction.

chapters.title: Ines, Alive Somewhere
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A postmarked letter arrives from coastal Wales containing a pressed fern and one line: 'Thank you for asking.' No return address. Coral chooses not to search further. Emotional beat: grace in letting the rescued stay free.

chapters.title: The New Catalogue
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, epilogue. He begins a new finding aid titled 'Hollowmere, Unsealed,' with Tamsin as apprentice archivist and Sunday dinners with the constable's family. The crypt is reopened as a memorial garden. Emotional beat: belonging, earned and chosen.
